title: The Rooftop Nibbler
markdown:
I practically bounced on the balls of my feet, ready to spill the beans. This was Rafi the roofer’s apprentice and Bit the jackdaw's absolute favorite day of the week: Saturday! Why? Because Saturday meant a rooftop picnic lunch! It was their special ritual, a reward for a week spent hauling buckets and hammering nails.

Rafi, a young lad with bright, curious eyes and hands as steady as the foundations he helped build, had climbed up to their usual spot. It was a wide, sunny ledge on the very tippy-top of the tallest building in town, the one that tickled the clouds. Bit, his sharp-witted, glossy-feathered sidekick, was already there, preening with a proud little flourish. "Caw! Caw!" he chirped, a sound that, if you understood jackdaw (and Rafi did, oh yes, he definitely did), meant, "Is it ready yet? Is it? My beak is practically watering!"

Rafi grinned, his heart as sturdy as the roofs he helped to build. He carefully pulled a bright red-and-white checkered blanket from his worn leather satchel. "Patience, my feathered friend!" he said, his voice warm and full of a roofer’s steady cheer. "Today, we have cheese and pickle sandwiches, the kind that make your tummy rumble with happiness, a crispy, juicy apple that shines like a ruby, and—wait for it—a whole jam tart!" He patted the satchel. "Enough for two, and a few extra crumbs for you, of course!"

They spread out their magnificent feast. The sun, a giant golden coin in the sky, warmed their faces. The city buzzed far below them like a sleepy bumblebee, its noises muffled by the height. Rafi took a huge, happy bite of his sandwich. Mmm, cheesy goodness that stretched just a little! He set it down for just a second to reach for his cool, fizzy lemonade.

"Hey!" he exclaimed, looking back with a surprised frown. A corner of his sandwich was gone! Not a big chunk, mind you, not a messy tear, but… a nibble. A perfect, tiny, impossibly neat, bite-sized nibble.

Bit hopped closer, his beady black eyes missing nothing, tilting his head so one eye seemed to ask, "Who did that?" He scanned the ledge. There was no one else around. No snooping cats, no stray dogs with rumbling bellies, not even a particularly bold pigeon looking for handouts.

Rafi chuckled, a sound like pebbles tumbling down a drainpipe (which, you know, is a very roofer-like chuckle). "Must have been a bit windy," he said, though he knew in his bones that wasn't quite right. The air was still and soft. He picked up his sandwich and took another bite. Delicious! He set it down again, more carefully this time.

WHOOSH! Another tiny nibble vanished! This time, it was from his bright red apple. A neat little crescent, gone in a flash, leaving a perfectly smooth edge behind.

"Okay, okay, okay, so then..." Rafi whispered, his eyes growing wide with a roofer’s focus, now on a different kind of construction. "This is seriously weird! Bit, did you see *that*?"

Bit let out a series of quick, questioning caws that sounded suspiciously like, "Did you see that?! It's like a magic sandwich! Where did it go?!" He’d seen *something*, or rather, he’d seen *nothing* happen, but the food was still disappearing as if by magic! It was like a culinary disappearing act!

"Right!" Rafi straightened up, his roofer’s brain, so good at figuring out tricky angles and loose tiles, kicking into high gear. This wasn't just a snack; it was a full-blown puzzle! A rooftop puzzle, no less! "We need a plan!"

He looked at the jam tart. It was a magnificent thing, a masterpiece of golden crust, bubbling like a tiny volcano with ruby-red jam. "This," he declared with a flourish, "is the main event. The star of the show! If someone's sneaking bites, they'll be after this!"

Bit puffed out his chest, his black feathers gleaming in the sun. He was ready for action. "Caw! Caw! Caw!" he agreed with gusto, which meant, "Lead the way, boss! We’ll get to the bottom of this!"

Rafi thought hard, tapping a finger against his chin. He couldn’t just chase the thief away; he wanted to know *who* it was! He looked around their sun-drenched perch. Nearby, a loose tile sat on the very edge of the roof, just begging to be nudged. Perfect!

"Bit, my friend," Rafi said, his voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper, a mischievous glint in his eye. "We're going to play a little trick! A roofer's special!"

He pulled a small, smooth, grey pebble from his pocket. It was the size of a large pea. "See that tile?" he pointed. "And see this pebble?" With great care, he placed the pebble right on top of the jam tart, like a tiny crown. Then, he gently nudged the loose tile so it balanced precariously on the edge. It wobbled ever so slightly.

"Now," Rafi whispered, his breath catching with excitement, "we hide! When our mystery nibbler comes, they'll try to grab the tart, they'll bump the tile, the tile will wobble, and the pebble will roll right down onto the roof with a CLATTER! That’ll tell us exactly where they are!"

Bit nodded enthusiastically, his head bobbing like a happy bobblehead. "Caw! CAW!" he squawked, which clearly meant, "Brilliant! Absolutely, fantastically brilliant! I’m already imagining the clatter!"

They scurried behind a sturdy, red-brick chimney, a cozy little hideaway. From there, they peeked out with all their might, their eyes like twin telescopes. The city sounds faded into a distant hum as they waited, their hearts beating with anticipation. Tick-tock, tick-tock went the invisible clock of excitement.

Suddenly, they heard a tiny rustle. It was so faint, it was almost lost in the breeze. Then, a quick, furtive movement near the picnic blanket. A small, furry head popped up, whiskers twitching like tiny antennae. It was a squirrel! A very cheeky-looking squirrel with bright, curious, beady eyes that darted around.

The squirrel, bold as brass, hopped onto the blanket. Its little paws, delicate and nimble, reached for the jam tart, its nose twitching at the sweet, sugary scent. Just as its tiny fingers brushed the golden crust, it bumped the wobbly tile!

CLATTER! The tile tipped with a surprising noise, and the pebble went rolling, landing with a distinct thud on the rooftop. The squirrel froze, its fur on end, utterly startled. It looked at the rolling pebble, then at the tantalizing tart, then up at the chimney where Rafi and Bit were hiding. It looked… caught red-pawed!

"Muahahaha!" Rafi couldn't help a little delighted chuckle, a sound that made Bit let out a triumphant, echoing "Caw-caw-CAW!"

The squirrel looked rather sheepish. It didn’t scamper away in a panic, though. It just sat there, looking a little bit guilty and a little bit hungry.

Rafi and Bit slowly stepped out from behind the chimney, their faces a mixture of surprise and amusement. The squirrel didn't move, its bushy tail twitching nervously, like it was trying to decide whether to make a run for it.

"Well now, Mr. Cheeky-Cheeks!" Rafi said gently, his voice soft and kind, like a warm hug. "You've been sneaking our lunch, haven't you?"

The squirrel chittered softly, a series of little squeaks and chirps, as if to say, "But it smelled SO good! And I was *so* hungry!"

Bit, ever the understanding friend, hopped forward. He nudged a small piece of sandwich crust towards the squirrel with his beak. "Caw?" he offered, a friendly question, which meant, "Here. Have some. We understand."

The squirrel cautiously sniffed the crust, its whiskers quivering with interest. Then, with a quick flick of its tiny tongue, it gobbled it down. Its tail gave a happy, grateful little flick.

Rafi smiled, a wide, warm smile that crinkled his eyes. "You know what?" he said to Bit, looking at the squirrel, who was now eyeing the jam tart with renewed interest. "This is much better than catching a thief. We have enough for a friend!" He carefully broke off a generous piece of sandwich and a chunk of apple. "Here you go, little nibbler. Plenty for everyone!"

The squirrel happily munched on the food, its earlier nervousness completely forgotten. It wasn't a thief, just a hungry little creature who liked delicious food as much as they did. And it was rather cute, Rafi had to admit.

From that day on, Rafi and Bit always saved a few extra crumbs and small pieces for their new friend, who they affectionately nicknamed Squeaky. The rooftop lunches were still their absolute favorite, a special time for delicious food and good company. But now, they were even more special, shared with a cheeky, furry friend and filled with the joy of a puzzle solved in the most delightful way. And Bit? Oh, he always kept an extra watchful eye, just in case any *other* delicious treats decided to mysteriously vanish! Caw! Caw! You never knew what exciting adventures awaited on a sunny rooftop!
characters: Rafi the roofer's apprentice, Bit the jackdaw
